headline: A session picker that shows what you asked
pill: the session picker shows what you actually asked
summary: Continuing a Claude Code or Codex session is easier. Each session in the picker is titled with the question you asked, not context the CLIs add behind the scenes, and the picker closes when you click away.

highlights.title: Titles you recognise
highlights.text: Claude Code and Codex quietly record extra context before your first message, such as which file was open in your editor. The picker used to show that. Now it skips it and shows the first thing you typed, without Markdown symbols or stray backslashes. The tool, its age and what happens when you pick it sit on one line underneath, so long titles no longer hide them. Press **Esc** or click anywhere outside to close the picker.
highlights.alt: The session picker listing four sessions titled with the questions asked, each with Claude Code or Codex and its age underneath

highlights.title: A proper button when there are no conversations yet
highlights.text: The empty Conversations view showed a stray `\n` in its message. It now reads cleanly, with a **Continue from a Claude Code or Codex Session** button underneath.
highlights.alt: The empty Conversations view with a short message and a blue Continue from a Claude Code or Codex Session button

improvements: The Marketplace page now has screenshots and a full overview of what Turnhuddle does.
